summary: Lunar-Si is an advanced full-stack web platform designed to streamline Artemis III mission planning. We developed an immersive 3D lunar exploration environment powered by React, Vite, and Three.js, backed by an asynchronous FastAPI server and a custom-trained ONNX machine learning model. The platform addresses the challenge by processing raw NASA LRO/LOLA binary topography data to evaluate multi-variable terrain parameters—such as micro-slopes, solar illumination, and Earth line-of-sight—across official lunar South Pole landing sites. Lunar-Si is vital because it bridges the gap between complex, raw geodetic data and intuitive decision-making, providing instant, physics-based safety scores and comprehensive environmental telemetry to ensure safe, efficient lunar landing site selection.
details:
Lunar-Si is an AI-powered interactive lunar exploration platform designed to support the evaluation and comparison of potential lunar landing sites, with a particular focus on the Moon's South Pole and future Artemis missions.

The project transforms complex lunar scientific data into an interactive 3D environment where users can explore the lunar surface, examine different landing locations, and evaluate their suitability based on multiple geological and environmental factors. It includes the nine official Artemis III candidate landing sites and allows users to select custom coordinates anywhere on the lunar surface for additional evaluation.

Lunar-Si works by integrating real topographical data derived from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) missions. The system processes elevation data, calculates terrain slopes, and applies mathematical polar corrections to improve the accuracy of terrain analysis near the lunar poles. It also evaluates important environmental conditions, including solar illumination, estimated daylight hours, Earth Line-of-Sight (LOS) for communication assessment, and proximity to potential water ice resources.

A custom-trained machine learning model is integrated into the platform to analyze multiple terrain and environmental parameters and generate an AI-based landing safety score ranging from 1% to 99%. The results are presented through an interactive 3D lunar globe, allowing users to explore locations and understand their potential advantages and challenges.

The project aims to make lunar landing-site analysis more accessible, interactive, and data-driven. It can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts understand the complex factors involved in lunar landing decisions. By combining geological analysis, environmental modeling, and artificial intelligence, Lunar-Si seeks to contribute to safer and more informed lunar mission planning.

Lunar-Si was developed using Python and JavaScript, with React and Vite for the frontend, Three.js and React Three Fiber for interactive 3D visualization, and FastAPI for backend development. The AI model is integrated using ONNX Runtime, while NumPy supports numerical and scientific calculations. Additional technologies include Pydantic, HTML, CSS, Git, and GitHub.

The project's creative aspect lies in combining real NASA lunar datasets, custom mathematical terrain processing, and a custom-trained AI model within a single interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying lunar maps or predefined landing locations, it enables users to investigate custom coordinates and receive multi-factor AI-based safety assessments. A particularly important technical feature is the use of latitude-based polar corrections to address geographic distortions near the lunar poles and improve terrain slope calculations.

Several factors were considered during development, including scientific accuracy, computational performance, accessibility, cost, and scalability. The platform relies on publicly available NASA datasets and software-based technologies, avoiding the need for expensive specialized hardware. Its architecture is designed to support efficient processing and interactive visualization while allowing future expansion with additional scientific datasets and environmental models.

Ultimately, Lunar-Si demonstrates how artificial intelligence, geospatial data processing, and interactive 3D technologies can work together to make lunar exploration analysis more understandable and support future human exploration of the Moon.
